paras.text: Effect of climate on human life
paras.urdu: آب و ہوا کا انسانی زندگی پر اثر:-
paras.pashto: پر انساني ژوند د اقلیم اغېز

paras.text: The effect of climate on human life is an established fact. If we glance at history it is clearly evident that ancient civilisations grew and flourished where the climate was extremely favourable for all aspects of human life. The scientific progress of the present age has tried to mould weather conditions to suit itself. But in spite of this, climate fully affects human health, way of living, business, habits, dress, thinking, customs and transport — in short every aspect of life.

Effect of climate on human life

The effect of climate on human life is an established fact. If we glance at history it is clearly evident that ancient civilisations grew and flourished where the climate was extremely favourable for all aspects of human life. The scientific progress of the present age has tried to mould weather conditions to suit itself. But in spite of this, climate fully affects human health, way of living, business, habits, dress, thinking, customs and transport — in short every aspect of life.

Pakistan is a vast country. There is no uniformity in its physical features. Mountains and plateaus are spread over 60 per cent of its total area, while the remaining part is plain and desert. In the same way its climate also differs from one part to another. In proportion to this difference there is also a difference in the distribution of population in the various areas and in the way of living and occupations of the people.

Economic imbalance

By economic imbalance is meant that our expenditure is greater and income less, or that the fulfilment of our needs of life is not possible within our income. For the last 73 years Pakistan has been suffering from economic imbalance, because income is less and expenditure greater. The reason for this is that our non-development expenditure is very high and development expenditure low. Our exports are less and imports more. Therefore the budget suffers from deficit, i.e. economic imbalance.

A large part of our budget consists of current expenditure. For example, in the budget of the financial year 2020–21, 41 per cent is the repayment of loans, 23 per cent defence expenditure and 25 per cent other current expenditure. In this way only 11 per cent of the budget is left for development expenditure, which is insufficient for the rapid progress of a developing country.

Causes of economic instability

At the time of the establishment of Pakistan the population was large and resources were not available. Pakistan was faced with unfavourable conditions, and the Pak–Bharat war of 1948 created further difficulties for Pakistan.

The Government of Pakistan began five-year programmes for development, thanks to which industries were promoted. Dams and canals were built for the development of agriculture. To improve the economic situation, help was taken from the international community, through which industry and agriculture progressed.

The Pak–Bharat wars of 1965 and 1971 once again badly affected our economy. Because of these conditions loans and interest on Pakistan kept increasing.

Our governments paid attention to increasing military strength to maintain their freedom, while the political process kept breaking at short intervals. Because the political process did not continue uninterrupted, neither could stability come to the country nor could an atmosphere of confidence be created among the people.

The policies of political parties also kept changing. Because of the policy of nationalisation industrial progress stopped. The problem of water shortage in the country became serious. There was also an electricity crisis, through which the confidence of industrialists was broken. Equal opportunities of progress could not be created in the provinces. Then the shadows of war also kept hovering over our land.

Pak–Bharat relations always remained bad over the Kashmir issue. Now both countries have become atomic powers, while the problems between them stand as they were. The United Nations and the international community also avoid mediating on an issue like Kashmir. In this situation the possibilities of setting up new industries and new investment kept diminishing. On the other hand the conditions of Afghanistan also kept negatively affecting our economy. Smuggling and drugs ruined our economy. Thus, instead of progressing, we kept being pressed under the burden of loans. Even today Pakistan is indebted by billions of dollars.

پاک بھارت تعلقات کشمیر کے مسئلے پر ہمیشہ خراب رہے۔ اب دونوں ممالک ایٹمی قوت بن چکے ہیں جبکہ ان کے درمیان مسائل جوں کے توں کھڑے ہیں۔ اقوامِ متحدہ اور عالمی برادری بھی کشمیر جیسے مسئلے پر ثالثی سے پرہیز کرتی ہے۔ اس صورت میں نئی صنعتیں لگانے اور نئی سرمایہ کاری کے امکانات کم ہوتے چلے گئے۔ دوسری طرف افغانستان کے حالات بھی ہماری معیشت پر منفی طور پر اثر انداز ہوتے رہے۔ سمگلنگ اور منشیات نے ہماری معیشت کو تباہ کر دیا۔ اس طرح ہم ترقی کے بجائے قرضوں کے بوجھ تلے دبتے چلے گئے۔ آج بھی پاکستان اربوں ڈالر کا مقروض ہے۔
